evidence.note: Only concrete verification the agent ever achieved was a single trivial 'return 42' program compiling/running plus a wrapper check; this is the sole positive data point in the whole trajectory.
First attempt to run the full 516-test suite; agent planned to 'examine which tests pass/fail' but the run hung and no pass count was ever produced.

For ~150 steps the agent repeatedly restated 'the full test suite (516 tests) has NOT been validated' and that the binary 'passes a basic return 42 test' — verbal awareness of unknown status but no structured pass/fail ledger, no aggregate count.
Final steps: still no test results obtained; agent never got two comparable data points, so regression detection never occurred and could not have.

reasoning: The agent knew the total test count (516/780) and consistently acknowledged its suite status was unvalidated, and it noted the one trivial test plus wrapper check that passed — placing it just above anchor 0. But it never obtained any actual pass count (the suite hung on first run and the rest of the trajectory was spent trying to un-stick the terminal), kept no structured view of what works vs. remains, and performed zero regression detection since it never had a second data point to compare. This falls short of anchor 3's 'occasionally notes a pass count,' landing at a 2.
